engines.note: claude --help on this host (2026-08-08) reports `-r, --resume [value]` ("Resume a conversation by session ID"). Matches what the hub already splices for the claude-code family.

codex resume --help on this host (2026-08-08) reports `codex resume [OPTIONS] [SESSION_ID] [PROMPT]`, SESSION_ID being a "Conversation/session id (UUID) or thread name". This is the CLI rung; our live codex path resumes over app-server `thread/resume` instead — see the `codex` family row.

agy --help on this host (2026-08-08) reports `--conversation` ("Resume a previous conversation by ID"). Matches spliceAntigravityResume and ADR-035 D8. herdr keys this engine `antigravity_cli`; the binary is `agy`.

families.note: The hub splices `--resume <id>` into backend.cmd before respawn (server/resume_splice.go, ADR-014).
ADR-035 D8. agy resumes interactively; the headless -p form hangs.

The engine HAS an argv recipe, but the hub is not what applies it. The hub injects the ACP `resume_session_id` field (handlers_sessions.go); the M2 exec-per-turn driver separately threads `--resume <UUID>` into each turn's argv from a cursor it captured itself (driver_exec_resume.go). So the argv row above documents driver-internal behaviour and feeds L3/L4 — it is not a spawn-time splice, and treating it as one would rewrite a cmd the hub has never rewritten.

Live path is app-server `thread/resume` (driver_appserver.go), fed by the top-level `resume_session_id` spec field. The `codex resume <id>` CLI recipe is the spawn-per-session fallback rung that vision-parity L4 names — real, but not what the hub drives today.
The retired Python family (#378). No new spawn can carry this kind, but rows persisted before the retirement still resume, so the row stays — dropping it would silently cold-start them.

Deliberately unmapped to herdr's `kimi` recipe. Our engine is the compiled-TypeScript Kimi CLI (ADR-054); herdr's `kimi --session <id>` may or may not be the same binary, and no one has run `kimi --help` on a host that has it. Our live path is ACP session/load, so nothing needs the argv today. To map it: probe the binary, then set `engine: kimi` and change that row's `verified` to `probe`.
